TASK: write tools/completion.mjs and tests/completion.test.mjs. This is zsh tab completion for the `swarm` command.

Read the one-line usage text near the top of main() in tools/swarm.mjs (search for 'Project Swarm\nUsage') to get the real commands and flags.

tools/completion.mjs must export:
- COMMANDS: an array of { name, summary, args, flags } for every top-level command in that usage text, plus `completion` and `help`. `args` is one of 'run' (takes a run id), 'manifest' (takes a .json file), 'provider' (takes one of the doctor provider names), 'goal' (free text), 'none'. `flags` is the list of --flags that command accepts, taken from the usage text. Summaries are one short plain sentence.
- PROVIDERS: the doctor provider names from the usage text.
- zshCompletion(): returns the text of a zsh completion file named _swarm. It must start with `#compdef swarm`, complete the command names with their summaries (_describe), complete each command's flags, complete run ids by calling `swarm __complete runs` in the current directory (one run id per line, newest first), complete *.json files for manifest arguments, and complete provider names for `doctor`. It must also work when the user ran `swarm --root DIR` first (pass --root DIR to `swarm __complete runs`). Keep the zsh simple and correct; avoid features that need compinit options beyond the defaults.
- completeRuns(root, { readdir }): returns run ids found in <root>/.swarm/runs (directory names only), newest first by name (run ids start with a millisecond timestamp), at most 200. A missing directory returns []. `readdir` is injectable for tests (default fs.promises.readdir).

Tests: COMMANDS has no duplicate names; every command named in the usage text of tools/swarm.mjs (read the file as text in the test and pull the names with a regex from the Usage line) is in COMMANDS, and every COMMANDS entry except completion/help/ticket/scaffold appears there; zshCompletion() starts with #compdef swarm, mentions every command name and `swarm __complete runs`; completeRuns sorts newest first, ignores files, caps at 200 and returns [] when the directory is missing. If `zsh` exists on the machine (spawnSync('zsh', ['-n', file]) status 0 when you write the script to a temp file), also assert that `zsh -n` accepts the script syntax; skip that one assertion when zsh is missing.

TASK: write tools/swarm-bin.mjs and tests/swarm-bin.test.mjs. This installs and checks a real `swarm` executable at ~/.local/bin/swarm, so agents and scripts (non-interactive shells that do not load aliases) can run `swarm`.

tools/swarm-bin.mjs must export:
- WRAPPER_MARKER: the string '# managed by project-swarm'.
- swarmBinPath(home): path.join(home, '.local', 'bin', 'swarm').
- wrapperText({ node, runner }): the text of a POSIX sh script. Line 1 `#!/bin/sh`, line 2 the marker, then: set NODE to the absolute node path given; if it is not executable fall back to `command -v node`; if still none print `swarm: node not found; reinstall project-swarm` to stderr and exit 127; finally `exec "$NODE" "<runner>" "$@"`. Quote paths safely (single-quote them and escape any single quote); reject a node or runner path containing a newline or NUL by throwing. The wrapper must not depend on PATH or on any shell startup file, because it runs in `env -i` shells.
- installSwarmCommand({ home, runner, node = process.execPath }): creates ~/.local/bin if needed, writes the wrapper with mode 0o755, and returns { status, path, runner, node, reason? } where status is 'installed' (new or changed), 'unchanged' (identical content already there) or 'refused' (a file or symlink exists at that path that does not carry the marker; never overwrite it; reason says so). It must be idempotent and must never write outside <home>/.local/bin.
- checkSwarmCommand({ home, env = process.env }): returns { path, installed, ours, runner, runnerExists, onPath, warnings }. `installed` is whether a file exists; `ours` whether it carries the marker; `runner` is the runner path parsed back out of the wrapper (or null); `runnerExists` whether that file exists; `onPath` whether the bin directory is one of the entries of env.PATH (compare resolved real paths, ignore empty entries). warnings is a list of strings, each starting with a stable code: `swarm-command-missing: run "swarm update" or tools/install.mjs --user to install it`, `swarm-command-foreign: <path> is not managed by project-swarm`, `swarm-command-stale-runner: <runner> is missing`, `swarm-not-on-path: add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to ~/.zshenv (zsh reads ~/.zshenv in non-interactive shells; ~/.zshrc is only for interactive ones)`.

Tests (all with a temp HOME and a stub runner file): installs once then 'unchanged'; refuses a foreign file and leaves it byte-identical; refuses a foreign symlink; the written file is executable; wrapperText throws on a newline in a path and survives a path with a space and a single quote; checkSwarmCommand covers missing, foreign, stale runner, not-on-path, and a clean install with the dir on PATH. Plus one end-to-end test: install a wrapper whose runner is a tiny .mjs that prints JSON of process.argv.slice(2), then run it with spawnSync('/bin/bash', ['-c', 'swarm a "b c"'], { env: { HOME: tmp, PATH: tmp + '/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin' } }) so node is NOT on that PATH, and assert it printed ["a","b c"] and exited 0.

TASK: write tools/status.mjs and tests/status.test.mjs. This is the data and text for running `swarm` with no arguments inside a project: a short status plus the 5 most useful next commands.

tools/status.mjs must export:
- async projectStatus(root, { env = process.env, now = Date.now, doctorAll, spendToday }): returns an object with exactly these keys:
  - root
  - initialized: true when <root>/.project-swarm.json exists
  - lastRun: null, or { id, status, startedAt, finishedAt, counts, costUsd } for the newest run found in <root>/.swarm/runs/*/state.json (newest by startedAt, falling back to the directory name); counts is state.summary.counts; costUsd comes from state.summary or sums job costUsd values that are numbers, else null. A run directory with unreadable state.json is skipped.
  - lanes: { up: [agent names], down: [agent names] } built from `await doctorAll()` (injected; it returns { providers: [{ agent, status }] }). Status 'compatible', 'configured' and 'reachable' count as up; everything else is down. If doctorAll throws, lanes is { up: [], down: [], error: message }.
  - spendToday: `await spendToday()` (injected; returns { usd, byLane } where byLane is an object of agent to usd); if it throws or is missing, { usd: null, byLane: {} }.
  - next: an array of exactly 5 strings, each a ready-to-run command, chosen by the situation: not initialized → starts with 'swarm init'; initialized with no runs → 'swarm "describe your goal in one sentence"' first; last run failed or cancelled → 'swarm inspect <id>' first; last run still running → 'swarm monitor <id> --watch' first; last run complete → 'swarm rollup <id> --text' first. Then fill to 5 from this fixed list, skipping duplicates: 'swarm doctor all', 'swarm board', 'swarm version --check', 'swarm scale', 'swarm help'.
- formatStatus(status): returns plain text of at most 14 lines: a first line `Project Swarm status for <root>`, then lines for: initialized (yes/no, and 'run: swarm init' when no), last run (id, status, how long ago as 'Xm ago'/'Xh ago'/'Xd ago' relative to a `now` option passed as formatStatus(status, { now }), counts, cost), lanes up (comma separated, or 'none'), lanes down (comma separated, or 'none'), today's spend ('$0.00' style, or 'unknown'), then a blank line and 'Next:' with the 5 commands each indented two spaces. No ANSI color. Plain short sentences.

Tests: a temp project with and without .project-swarm.json; no runs; a failed run, a running run, a complete run (check the first next command each time and that next always has 5 unique entries); newest run wins when two exist; a corrupt state.json is skipped; doctorAll throwing gives the error shape; spendToday missing gives usd null; formatStatus output has no more than 14 lines, includes the commands, and prints 'unknown' for null spend.
